title: [Bug][XPU]: Silent persistent output corruption (endless "!" / token 0) under sustained concurrent decode on Arc Pro B70, W4A16 27B head_dim 256
body:
## Summary

A W4A16 (compressed-tensors, group 128, symmetric) 27B Qwen-family model served on a single Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage, 32GB, xe driver) intermittently degenerates into emitting only "!" tokens (token id 0) under sustained concurrent decode. The corruption is silent: HTTP 200, finish_reason length, zero dmesg events, container healthy, /v1/models fine. It is PERSISTENT: after load drops, even fresh single-request generations return only "!" until the engine is restarted. Engine restart fully recovers (weight reload), which points at long-lived VRAM state (weights or a persistent workspace) being corrupted in place.

It struck our production engine four times in ~30 hours (three times at <= 4 concurrent requests after hours of sustained load; once within ~10 minutes when 12 concurrent synthetic streams mixed with real long-prompt traffic). Two sibling W4A16 models (14B and 8B, head_dim 128) on the same silicon under continuous scoring load have never corrupted in weeks, including c=12 stress sweeps.

The everything-token-0 signature suggests logits collapsing to NaN/zero (argmax degenerates to index 0), i.e. numeric poisoning of something persistent rather than per-request state.

## Environment

- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B70 32GB (Battlemage); reproduced on TWO different physical cards (VM, VFIO passthrough), so not a single-card hardware fault
- Host: kernel 6.17.0-41-generic, xe driver
- Image: intel/vllm:0.21.0-ubuntu24.04-20260805 (vLLM 0.21.1.dev18+g8df6feb7d)
  - torch 2.11.0+xpu, triton_xpu 3.7.0, vllm_xpu_kernels 0.1.8.2, dpcpp_cpp_rt 2025.3.2
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B fine-tune, W4A16 AutoRound -> compressed-tensors (group_size 128, symmetric, no g_idx), hidden 5120, 64 layers, head_dim 256, GQA 24/4, vocab 248320, lm_head unquantized
- Serve: --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype auto --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 --max-num-seqs 4..12 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048, no prefix caching
- Startup selects XPUwNa16LinearKernel (torch.ops._xpu_C.int4_gemm_w4a16) for CompressedTensorsWNA16; FLASH_ATTN (FA2) backend

## Fastest observed onset

Ramped concurrency sweep (cover-letter-shaped requests, max_tokens 700, 150s per level, c = 1, 2, 4, 8, 12) against the production engine while real traffic (6.7k-7.8k-token prompts, 2k-token completions) was also landing:

| c  | gen tok/s | mean e2e | garbage responses |
|----|-----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1  | 11.9      | 25.2s    | 0 |
| 2  | 26.0      | 24.4s    | 0 |
| 4  | 52.6      | 22.1s    | 0 |
| 8  | 102.6     | 23.3s    | 0 |
| 12 | 167.0     | 50.3s    | 36/36 (all "!") |

After the load stopped, a single-stream probe still returned 60 tokens of "!". Zero dmesg events throughout. Restart recovered.

## Isolation runs (all CLEAN, which is what makes this hard)

Each row is a separate fresh engine on the same hardware, 4-15 minute runs:

| model | image | gpu-mem-util | workload | result |
|-------|-------|--------------|----------|--------|
| 27B | dev18 | 0.90 | cold c=12, 133 reqs | clean |
| 27B | dev17 (intel/vllm:latest, 20260625 build) | 0.90 | cold c=12, 129 reqs | clean |
| 27B | dev17 | 0.97 | cold c=12, 134 reqs | clean |
| 27B | dev17 | 0.97 | full ramp c=1..12 | clean |
| 27B | dev18 | 0.97 | full ramp c=1..12 (exact replication of the corrupting run, minus live traffic) | clean |
| 27B | dev18 | 0.97 | 10 short-decode streams + 2 long-prompt (7k-token, chunked prefill) streams, 6 min | clean |
| 14B W4A16 head_dim 128 | dev18 | 0.5 | cold c=12, 239 reqs | clean |

So no single factor (image build, gpu-memory-utilization, ramp history, or a naive mixed prefill+decode workload) deterministically reproduces it from a cold engine in minutes. Production hit it four times in 30 hours. It behaves like a race whose probability rises steeply with decode batch depth and with real-traffic batch compositions.

## What we ruled out

- Hardware: identical corruption on two different physical cards; a c=12 sweep on the second card corrupted the same way while weeks of equal-wattage load from the head_dim-128 models never did. Power delta between clean c=8 (195W) and corrupting c=12 (199W) is ~2%.
- The int4 GEMM kernel in isolation: a standalone harness driving torch.ops._xpu_C.int4_gemm_w4a16 with this model's exact layer shapes (5120x8192, 6144x5120, 5120x34816, 17408x5120, group 128) at M = 1..32, 64, 128, 512, 2048 shows no NaN/Inf, bit-exact determinism across repeated calls, no input-buffer mutation (weight/scale checksums stable), and no cross-call poisoning of a baseline M=1 result.
- vLLM Python-level differences: the dev17 and dev18 images' /opt/vllm/vllm trees are byte-identical except _version.py and an API-middleware helper; torch/triton/vllm_xpu_kernels/dpcpp versions are identical. (We initially suspected a build regression; the tree diff killed that.)
- KV preemption: vLLM logged zero preemptions in all runs (KV was never near full; 172k-token cache vs ~10-40k in flight).

## Notes that may help localize it

- head_dim 256 + GQA 24/4 is the standout difference from our never-corrupting 14B/8B (head_dim 128) neighbors; vllm_xpu_kernels 0.1.8.2 predates the v0.1.9 mixed-batch attention rework.
- vocab 248320 means the (unquantized bf16) lm_head GEMM's M equals the decode batch depth; corruption onset correlates with deeper decode batches.
- The corruption survives across requests but not restarts: whatever is poisoned lives in VRAM for the process lifetime (weights, persistent workspace, or compiled-graph buffers).
- Ubuntu 24.04 HWE-class host kernel with xe; the same box previously produced GP-fault/BCS-reset issues under TP=2 (#41663) but this failure mode has no driver-visible events at all.

## Ask

We are happy to run instrumented builds, extra logging, or targeted experiments on this hardware; the model and full configs can be shared. Detection guidance for other users: only a CONTENT probe catches this (health endpoints and /v1/models keep answering normally); we run a cron that generates a short completion every 10 minutes and restarts on "!" output.

Mitigation we are validating: moving the affected engine to the 20260625 build at gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 (every isolation cell on that config was clean, and it is ~20% faster on this model: 14.8 vs 11.9 tok/s single-stream, 154.9 tok/s at c=12).
